caption: Isla Bastimentos National Marine Park, created in 1988 in the Bocas del Toro archipelago, was Panama's first marine park and protects coral reefs, mangroves and island forest.

landmark: Silbo Gomero whistled language, La Gomera
caption: Silbo Gomero, a whistled form of Spanish used on La Gomera in the Canary Islands, was added to UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009.
Curiepe, in Venezuela's Barlovento region, is an Afro-Venezuelan community known for its drums and for its San Juan Bautista festival, celebrated around 23 to 25 June.
The Cayapas-Mataje Ecological Reserve protects mangrove forest on Ecuador's northern coast near the Colombian border and is known for some of the tallest mangrove trees in the world.

city: Triunfo de la Cruz, near Tela
landmark: Triunfo de la Cruz Garifuna community
caption: Triunfo de la Cruz is a Garifuna community on Honduras's Caribbean coast; UNESCO proclaimed the Garifuna language, dance and music a masterpiece of intangible heritage in 2001.
The wooden Church of Achao on Quinchao Island is one of 16 churches of Chiloé that were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2000.
The Museo de las Culturas Afromestizas in Cuajinicuilapa, on Guerrero's Costa Chica, is described as the first museum in Mexico devoted to the history of Afro-Mexican communities.
The Casa Nacional de Moneda in Potosí, where coining began in 1773, is part of the city's UNESCO World Heritage listing, granted in 1987.
Castillo San Cristóbal, begun in 1634 to defend Old San Juan against land attack, is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 1983.
Gaiman, in Argentina's Chubut valley, is known for its Welsh tea houses, a tradition linked to the Welsh settlers who arrived in Patagonia on the ship Mimosa in 1865.
